teaser.en: Every Digo kitchen needs a *mwiko* for stirring ugali, and this bush shrub is named as the maker of them.

summary.en: *Mtsonga mwiko* is a bush shrub with long-tubed white flowers. Its branches are carved into *mwiko*, the cooking sticks used for stirring.

about.en: *Mtsonga mwiko* is a shrub with white flowers that have long, slender tubes, opening at the tip into a star of narrow petals. After flowering it forms lobed capsules that split open to release the seeds.

uses.en: Its branches are carved into cooking sticks, *mwiko*, the flat wooden stirrers used in the kitchen.

culture.en: The name means 'maker of cooking sticks', after its main use. It is one of several Digo plant names that describe exactly what the plant is good for.

names.en: The Digo name is *mtsonga mwiko*. No Swahili or English common name has been recorded; botanists call it *Turraea nilotica*.

reason.en: Bushveld gardenia, also made into cooking stirrers
Another plant named after what is made from it

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: an ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD thesis, Univ. Bayreuth, Appendix III (Digo–botanical name list) & Appendix VI (name semantics). https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
